summary.text: 哥 is traditionally analyzed as two 可, with 可 supplying a sound cue. The graph was also used for 謌, “song,” but the reason for that use is unclear. Its common meaning is “elder brother”; this kinship sense is not shown to have developed from the song use.

formation.text: The received analysis describes 哥 as formed from two 可. Historical sound comparison supports a phonetic role for 可, though the analysis does not explain what the doubled form depicts or why it was formed this way. The proposed mouth-and-breath or singing picture is speculative.

components.text: The traditional analysis identifies two 可 in 哥; 可 serves as a phonetic element here. Early forms of 可 are described as containing 口 and 丂, but its original referent is unsettled. The selected oracle-style and Shuowen seal-style images show 可, not standalone 哥.

sound.text: In the Zhengzhang Old Chinese reconstruction, 可 and 哥 share a rhyme but differ in initial and tone, supporting a historical sound relationship rather than identical pronunciation.

history.text: The received Shuowen analysis names two 可 and records that 哥 was used for 謌. The selected oracle-style and Shuowen seal-style illustrations are modern redrawings of 可, not standalone forms of 哥, and do not show a sequence of 哥’s historical forms.
Early bronze and manuscript examples of 謌 and related song graphs do not securely attest standalone 哥, so they do not date or trace the development of 哥’s stacked form.

uncertainties.text: The suggestion that the stacked form depicts a mouth and breath, or began as a picture of singing, is speculative. The analysis supports 可 as a sound element in song-related graphs and records the use of 哥 for 謌, but does not identify 可’s original referent or establish a singing picture for 哥.

Written kinship use is reported from Tang-era material. Proposed borrowing routes differ: one derives the word from Xianbei *aqa via 阿哥; another proposes a Turkic-mediated route and rejects direct derivation from the recorded transcription 啊干. The source word’s native pronunciation and the transmission steps remain uncertain.
Available accounts do not provide a complete chronology for the uses “elder brother,” “father,” or broader forms of address, or establish that kinship uses developed from the song use.

senses.text: The received Shuowen entry glosses 哥 as “sound”; a later note says this sense was no longer in use at the annotator’s time. This gloss does not establish the character’s earliest meaning.

senses.gloss: song; to sing (use of 哥 for 謌/歌)
senses.period: Han-era use reported; precise earliest attestation unresolved

senses.text: 哥 is used for “elder brother,” with written kinship use reported from Tang-era material. Its proposed borrowing origin is disputed, and the sense is not shown to derive from the song use.
Historical accounts report use for “father” and broader male address, but do not establish a complete chronology or a secure development from “elder brother.”

limitations.text: Song-related and kinship uses are treated as distinct word histories represented by the same graph; a semantic chain connecting them is not established.
The proposed foreign origin of the kinship word remains unsettled; the source-language pronunciation and adaptation route are not established by the cited accounts.

items.period: Shang oracle-script tradition; conventionally c. 13th–11th centuries BCE
items.tradition: Shang oracle-script style; modern vector redraw
items.caption: 可 in a modern redraw of an oracle-script form, included as a visual example of the component that Shuowen says forms 哥. The image is not an attested standalone form of 哥.
items.alt: Black oracle-script-style rendering of 可, with a long slanting upper stroke and a lower boxlike form.
items.selection_reason: The candidate makes the 可 component visible, which helps explain the traditional analysis of 哥 as formed from two 可. The original referent of 可 and the earliest graphic origin of 哥 remain uncertain.

items.period: Shuowen seal-script tradition; received lexicographic form associated with the Han dynasty
items.tradition: Shuowen seal style; modern vector redraw
items.caption: 可 in a modern redraw of a Shuowen-style seal form. It illustrates the component named in the traditional analysis of 哥, not a dated standalone form of 哥.
items.alt: Black seal-script-style rendering of 可, with a horizontal top stroke, a small enclosed shape beneath it, and a long curving stroke descending below.
items.selection_reason: This complements the oracle-style component example by showing 可 in the received Shuowen seal-script tradition. It does not establish a chronological sequence for standalone 哥.

limitations.text: Both images depict 可, not 哥, and are modern redrawings rather than photographs of ancient artifacts. The evidence does not establish a reliable dated sequence of standalone 哥 forms or the earliest origin of its stacked shape.

Shuowen analyzes 哥 as formed from two 可 and records its use for 謌, but this does not establish what the earliest form depicted. A mouth-and-breath or singing-origin interpretation for the stacked shape remains speculative.
